findings.reason: the followup is the plan's dispatch chain, so without a new followup naming §33 to §35 the work is invisible to the coordinator and stalls exactly as f-wftl-006, -007 and -008 did before each was rewritten.
findings.text: f-wftl-009 is the plan's only open followup and its title and body name §9, §22, §30, §31 and §32, while this version adds §33, §34 and §35 as implementable (plan.html:23); a coordinator driving the plan from its open followup with the recommended invocation (`/reckon-build work-flows-to-the-lane §32`) dispatches nothing for the three new sections, and they sit unbuilt behind a chain that reads complete

findings.reason: a worker implementing this case literally builds a gc that skips ended runs, contradicting the deliverable it is meant to gate, and the correct assertion (gc removes ended-run residue and touches no live run's worktree or directory) has to be stated before the node can pass.
findings.text: §34's last done-when case requires that "a gc pass over a crew home holding 200 ended runs and 5 live ones touches only the 5 live runs' paths", but the same section's Deliverable makes the sweep a backstop that cleans what ended runs left behind and states the bounded population is achieved by runs removing their own residue, so a gc that touches only live runs' paths would never remove the 200 ended runs' worktrees or directories and the population the Deliverable bounds would not stay bounded

findings.reason: a worker implementing the Deliverable's single sentence fails its own gate on the case the earlier review added, and the two outcomes differ in substance (a scheduler that exists and refused versus one that was never named), so the Deliverable must split them rather than the gate being weakened.
findings.text: §30's Deliverable states one row text for two different conditions — "When it could not be asked, or the wait names no job, the row says the scheduler was not consulted" — while the done-when requires the un-queryable case's row to say "the scheduler could not be asked", a different sentence for the same field

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the write paths named by s30, s31, s32, s33, s34 and s35 all exist at b575b660a0 (`reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py`, `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py`, `reckon/crew/queue_landing.py`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py`, `reckon/crew/resumption.py`, `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, `reckon/cli.py`, `reckon/crew/pending_landing.py`, `reckon/ledger.py`), and the cited plans `a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline` (§74, §78 and §79 present), `concurrent-edits-meet-at-the-merge` and `crew-state-stays-bounded` all resolve under `docs/plans/`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §34's (plan.html:198) gc case asserts a gc pass "touches only the 5 live runs' paths" over a home holding 200 ended runs, which is the inverse of the backstop the same section's Deliverable describes; and §30's (plan.html:182) un-queryable-scheduler case requires a row text the Deliverable does not state.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — no section writes a gate log, measurement or figure to a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary directory; s30 to s35 cite the section's evidence fragment and s9 names the durable record `docs/evidence/archive/work-flows-to-the-lane-landed.html`, and the live-fleet measurements in s32, s34 and s35 are recorded there rather than in `/tmp`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s30 to s35 name no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag as a symbol; the tokens the sections do carry (`run-producer-gone`, `held-on-claim`, `promotion-requested`) are existing data values the section explicitly says keep their names, and no comment explains itself by a plan item.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — each section's stated root cause is the one its cited evidence shows: s30's row asserting no job is alive without asking the scheduler matches the probe form it quotes; s31's promotion deleting the live pointer matches the silent resume it records; s34's and s35's populations match the counts they cite and the reading they attribute to the py-spy dumps, and no section prescribes a code path, step sequence or formula (the write paths name modules to touch, not functions or algorithms).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s30 names one endpoint (a scheduler wait is not read as abandoned while a job is alive) with the row-wording clarification serving that same endpoint; s31 couples the hold and the resume refusal through one mechanism, since the resume takes the hold as its first act; s32 to s35 each name one endpoint.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the plan's only open followup, f-wftl-009 (plan.html:254-257), names §9, §22, §30, §31 and §32 while this version newly declares §33, §34 and §35 implementable, and no followup names them.
